overview: Sous-Storefront is a server-rendered React e-commerce storefront where shoppers browse products by category, manage a persistent cart, and complete a simulated checkout. It runs on React Router v7 with TanStack Query for data fetching, all powered by the public DummyJSON API and persisted to browser localStorage via Zustand stores.
structure_narrative:
## Three Runtime Boundaries

The storefront spans **server**, **browser**, and **external** — three distinct runtime boundaries following the C4 Container model. There is no backend of its own, no database, and no authentication. The server is a rendering layer, not an application server.

## Server

**root-layout-loader**, **home-loader**, and **products-loader** run on Node 20 Alpine via react-router-serve. They prefetch data from **dummyjson**, dehydrate TanStack Query caches, and ship pre-rendered HTML to the browser. The routes `/` and `/products` are also prerendered at build time for instant cold loads.

## Browser

After hydration, the **browser** takes full control — client-side routing, infinite scroll pagination, cart management via **cart-store**, and theme toggling through **theme-store**. All UI composition flows through **app-root** down to shared components and **ui-primitives** built on Radix.

## External

The **external** boundary holds **dummyjson** (the sole data source, with no SLA), **localstorage** (persistence for both Zustand stores), and the **dom** (direct classList mutation for instant theme switching). Every byte of product data originates from DummyJSON — if it goes down, the storefront goes dark.

data_flows.name: SSR Prefetch & Hydration
data_flows.narrative:
**root-layout-loader** fires first, creating a fresh QueryClient and calling prefetchQuery on **categories-query** — fetching the full category list from **dummyjson** via **api-client**.

**home-loader** runs next. It awaits the categories, then calls prefetchInfiniteQuery on **category-sections-query** to warm the first page — 4 categories, 4 products each. **products-loader** does the same for /products, prefetching 8 products in a single query.

Each loader dehydrates its QueryClient into serialized state. On the client, **app-root** wraps everything in QueryClientProvider, and HydrationBoundary rehydrates the cache. TanStack Query hooks read from warm cache on first render — zero waterfalls, no loading flash.

data_flows.name: Client-Side Browsing
data_flows.narrative:
Once hydrated, the shopper browses entirely client-side. **home-page** uses an intersection observer to detect when the user scrolls near the bottom, triggering fetchNextPage on **category-sections-query** — which pages through categories in batches of 4 via **api-client** to **dummyjson**. Each batch loads with an artificial 800ms delay baked into the query function.

On /products, **products-page** uses **products-query** with a Load more button for manual pagination, 8 products at a time. **nav-menu** reads **categories-query** (already warm from SSR) to list all browsable categories.

Clicking a category triggers a client-side route transition to /products/:category. The entire browsing experience stays within TanStack Query's cache — re-visiting a category page finds warm data rather than re-fetching.

data_flows.name: Cart Lifecycle
data_flows.narrative:
A shopper clicks Add to cart on a **product-card**. The onAddToCart callback calls addItem on **cart-store**, which upserts the product into the items array and recomputes the total. A sonner toast confirms the action.

The **cart-drawer** in the header reactively reflects the new state — showing the item with quantity controls. **cart-item-component** handles increment, decrement, and remove. Clicking Checkout navigates to **checkout-page**, which runs a clientLoader guard: empty cart redirects to **products-page**.

The checkout two-column layout renders **order-summary** alongside **shipping-form** and **payment-form**. On submit, clientAction simulates order processing with a 1-second delay, calls clear() on **cart-store**, sets the successfulOrder flag, and redirects to **success-page**.

**success-page** checks that flag via clientLoader — redirecting away if absent — then clears it and fires a confetti animation. Throughout this flow, **cart-store** persists to **localstorage** via Zustand's persist middleware, so cart state survives page refreshes.

data_flows.name: Theme Toggle
data_flows.narrative:
On page load, **app-root** runs a useEffect that imperatively reads **theme-store** — outside React's render cycle to avoid hydration mismatch — and applies the persisted dark or light class to document.documentElement.

When a shopper clicks **theme-toggle**, it calls setTheme on **theme-store**. The store does two things simultaneously: updates Zustand state (triggering re-renders of subscribers like the Sonner Toaster) and directly mutates the **dom** classList for instant CSS variable switching.

The persist middleware writes the preference to **localstorage**, so returning visitors see their chosen theme immediately without a flash of the wrong mode.

data_flows.name: Route Navigation
data_flows.narrative:
React Router v7 organizes the app into a nested route tree. **app-root** renders an Outlet that, for / and /products paths, resolves to **root-layout** — which provides the shared **header** with nav, cart, and theme controls.

For /checkout and /success, the Outlet bypasses **root-layout** entirely, rendering standalone pages without the header. This is a deliberate design choice — checkout is a focused flow with no distractions.

Within **root-layout**, a second Outlet renders either **home-page** (as index) or **products-page** (as child). Client-side guards on **checkout-page** and **success-page** use clientLoader to enforce state preconditions: checkout requires a non-empty cart, success requires the successfulOrder flag. Both redirect to **products-page** when their guard fails.

data_flows.name: E2E Test Coverage
data_flows.narrative:
**test-products** covers the browsing journey: product display by category (checking breadcrumb and card anatomy), the add-to-cart flow (toast notification, **cart-drawer** opening, item verification), and category navigation via the **nav-menu** drawer.

**test-checkout** covers the full purchase path. Starting from **products-page**, it adds a product, opens **cart-drawer**, navigates to **checkout-page**, fills both **shipping-form** and **payment-form**, submits the order, and verifies **success-page** renders correctly.

These 4 tests run across chromium, firefox, and webkit via GitHub Actions CI on every push to main.

state.name: Cart Store
state.narrative:
Cart state lives in **cart-store**, a Zustand store persisted to **localstorage** under the key cart-storage. There is no server-side cart — contents are device-local and ephemeral. This is a deliberate trade-off for a demo storefront with no backend.

The store holds an items array (product + quantity pairs), a computed total (recomputed via reduce on every mutation — a minor inefficiency noted as tech debt), and a successfulOrder boolean flag that bridges the checkout-to-success transition.

Five actions mutate state: addItem performs upsert, removeItem/incrementItem/decrementItem modify quantities, and clear resets everything. The successfulOrder flag is a coordination mechanism — **checkout-page** sets it before redirecting, and **success-page** reads and clears it as a one-time gate.
state.purpose: source-of-truth for cart contents and checkout coordination

state.name: Theme Store
state.narrative:
Theme preference lives in **theme-store**, also Zustand-persisted to **localstorage** (key: theme-storage). The store tracks a single value: dark, light, or system.

The interesting design choice is dual-write: setTheme both updates Zustand state (for React subscribers) and directly mutates **dom** classList on documentElement. This avoids a flash of wrong theme during React's render cycle.

**app-root** reads the store imperatively (not via hook) on mount to apply the initial class. The Sonner Toaster in **ui-primitives** subscribes reactively for toast theming.

state.name: TanStack Query Cache
state.narrative:
The query cache is the third state container, managed by TanStack Query rather than Zustand. **app-root** creates a fresh QueryClient per request — important for SSR, where a shared client would leak state between users.

SSR loaders populate the cache via prefetchQuery/prefetchInfiniteQuery, and HydrationBoundary transfers that state to the client. Once hydrated, the cache governs staleness, refetching, and garbage collection.

Three query families share the cache: **categories-query** (warm across most pages), **category-sections-query** (home page infinite scroll), and **products-query** (products page pagination). Because the cache is in-memory and per-tab, navigating between categories reuses cached data — but closing the tab loses everything.
state.purpose: server-state cache for DummyJSON API data

failure_modes.narrative:
DummyJSON starts returning 5xx errors. **api-client** has no retry policy, no timeout, and no circuit breaker — so requests hang indefinitely.

On the server, **root-layout-loader**, **home-loader**, and **products-loader** block waiting for a response that never comes. SSR stalls and the site becomes unresponsive. On the client, TanStack Query's default retry (3 attempts) provides some resilience for subsequent fetches, but the initial SSR-blocking request has no protection.

There is no fallback UI. Error boundaries exist in **app-root** but they show generic 404/error displays, not graceful degradation. The fix requires three changes: ky timeout (e.g., 5s), ky retry for transient failures, and per-route error boundaries with meaningful error states.

cascade.effect: nav menu has no categories to display

detection: No structured logging for request failures
recovery: Requires DummyJSON to recover — no fallback data source
Browser hard refresh after API recovers

failure_modes.narrative:
**localstorage** is full or unavailable — private browsing in some browsers, or storage quota exceeded. The Zustand persist middleware in **cart-store** and **theme-store** silently fails to write.

The stores still function in-memory for the current session, but cart contents and theme preference are lost on page refresh. This is graceful degradation by default — Zustand's persist middleware catches storage errors.

The user gets no indication that their cart will not survive a refresh. A toast or banner warning would prevent surprise data loss.

cascade.effect: cart state not persisted across refreshes

detection: No monitoring — silent failure by design
recovery: Stores recover automatically when storage becomes available

failure_modes.narrative:
**shipping-form** and **payment-form** use only HTML required attributes for validation — no schema validation via Zod or similar. **checkout-page** clientAction trusts whatever the browser submits.

In the current demo this is harmless — the backend is simulated. But any future real backend integration inherits unvalidated input.

A malicious or buggy form submission could send malformed data that a real payment processor would reject or, worse, process incorrectly. Adding Zod schemas before clientAction processes the form is the minimum fix.

failure_modes.narrative:
DummyJSON responds slowly but does not error. **home-loader** makes multiple sequential API calls — categories first, then 4 product fetches for the first page of category sections. The artificial 800ms delay in **category-sections-query** compounds the problem.

Without a timeout, a slow DummyJSON response (say 10s per request) means the home page SSR takes 40+ seconds. The user sees a blank page or browser timeout with no indication of progress.

**products-loader** is less affected (single query) but still blocks indefinitely. The fix: set ky timeout (e.g., 5000ms), remove the artificial delay, and consider streaming SSR for progressive rendering.
